invocation.output:
I ran the command exactly as given, and the `#` was interpreted by the shell as the start of a comment. So the effective command was `touch build.log`, and `# ci-marker` was ignored as a comment.

However, the shell wrapper behaved oddly: three files now exist:

| File | Size |
|---|---|
| `build.log` | 0 bytes |
| `ci-marker` | 0 bytes |
| `#` | 0 bytes |

Plus `.` and `..` (directories).

So the directory actually contains: `build.log`, `ci-marker`, and a file literally named `#`.

The intent was clearly to create only `build.log`. The extra `#` and `ci-marker` files appear because the commentary text was somehow passed along as arguments, most likely due to how the executor tokenized the string. Would you like me to delete `#` and `ci-marker` so only `build.log` remains? I won't touch anything unless you confirm.
